confirmed.description: The music-note glyph that stands for the bells is drawn on top of the first caption and overlaps the word 'prayer'. Art should not overlap the lettering.

confirmed.description: The long 'How many guards...' caption sits across the gutter between inset 2 (key ring) and inset 3 (boots on the stair). confirmed.description: Duarte's off-panel balloon points the wrong way. confirmed.description: The calluses on Duarte's right hand are not drawn, though the script says 'Draw the calluses on his right hand clearly' and the caption on this panel names them. Zoomed in, it shows ink spots on the fingertips and palm, which fits the bible's 'ink-stained fingers'. There are no callus pads under the fingers or on the heel of the hand. Why minor: the palm is about 110 px wide at 300 DPI, roughly 0.37 in when printed. Calluses at that size would be about 2 mm and hard to see even if drawn. The caption still delivers the soldier-past beat, and nothing in the art contradicts it. Fixing it would mean making the hand bigger or moving it forward, which is polish rather than a redraw. The reviewer's other points mostly do not hold. Only the very top of Duarte's hair touches the frame, and his whole face is visible. confirmed.description: The insert that should show his name being taken does not show the act. The script wants a tight shot of a clerk's hand writing a fresh, wet entry. Instead this is a medium still life of the whole desk, and its top third is a mostly empty caption box. The entry '17 prisioneiro marata' is set in clean Georgia italic like printed type, alone on the LEFT page, while the quill writes on the blank RIGHT page. Nothing ties the hand to the entry, and no ink is wet.
confirmed.evidence: On page 1 panel 2 the caption box spans y=595-780 with two lines of text. The ledger text sits at about x=320-520,y=1030. The quill nib touches the empty right-hand page at about x=905,y=1075.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed from a full-resolution crop of page 1, panel 1.2. The script asks for a tight insert of a clerk's hand writing "a number, then the words prisioneiro marata" with "the ink is still wet." The render does not show that:
(1) It is a medium shot of the whole desk: inkwell, map, bookshelf, a window onto Goa, and the full open ledger. The narration caption box fills about the top third of the panel (roughly y=825-1085 in original pixels), mostly as empty white space around two lines of text.
(2) "17 prisioneiro marata" is set in a clean typeset serif italic, like printed type. It floats alone on the left page.
(3) The quill nib touches the blank right-hand page at about x=1250,y=1490 (original pixels). There is no stroke, no ink trail and no wet sheen under it. The hand is not writing the entry, and nothing shows fresh ink.
Neither the continuity bible nor the cast overrides mention a ledger or say anything about 1.2, so nothing excuses the change.
The core beat still reads: a prisoner number in a book and a clerk's hand with a quill. So this is not a blocker. It is clearly wrong but limited to this one panel: the hand is cut off from the entry, there is no wet ink, the shot is not tight, and the entry looks printed. Major.

confirmed.description: The script marks page turns after both page 4 and page 7, and those pages have opposite parity. In a 9-page run starting on a recto, page 7 (recto) to page 8 is a true turn. Page 4 (verso) and page 5 (recto) would face each other as a spread, so the chamber reveal on page 5 sits beside page 4. This breaks 'Withhold the room until the turn' and 'This is the reveal the turn was built for.' Either a page must be added or moved, or the chapter must open on a verso.
confirmed.evidence: Folios 4 and 5 are consecutive even and odd pages. The script lines '*Page turn.*' follow both PAGE 4 and PAGE 7. Page 5 panel 1 is the full chamber reveal.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed. The folios printed on the renders show the clash. Page 1 is the chapter opener with folio 1, so it is a recto, and pages 4 and 5 carry folios 4 and 5, so they face each other as one spread. Page 4 does its job: panel 4.4 shows only the doorway and red glow, and the room stays hidden. But panel 5.1, the two-thirds-page chamber reveal with the vault, ropes, brazier and tool table, sits on the facing recto. A reader sees it while still reading page 4. That breaks the script's "Withhold the room until the turn" and "This is the reveal the turn was built for".

The script marks page turns after both page 4 and page 7, and those are pages of opposite parity, so only one of them can ever be a real turn. With the current folios, 7 to 8 is the true turn. PRODUCTION-PLAN.json says final folios are set at assembly after the front matter. Changing the parity there does not fix this: it moves the failure to the 7/8 spread, where the nod and the torture wide shot on page 8 would face João's line on page 7. The reviewer's "open on a verso" remedy fails for the same reason. The real fix is structural: the two turns must come after pages of the same parity, for example by adding or cutting one page between 5 and 7, or by moving the page-4 beats.

Nothing here is a redraw, a wrong identity or a missing beat. The beat is present but its surprise is spoiled by the facing page, which is clearly visible at print size. Major is the right severity.

refuted.description: In the Kanka memory inset, Nagoji is off-model. His moustache is thin and short, not the thick curled moustache on the sheet, and stubble runs along his jaw and chin. The memory is set before his capture, and the bible allows stubble only in captivity ('CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN (light stubble at most, captivity only)'). The face is also leaner and sharper than the present-day face beside it, which weakens the link the reader has to make between the two.
refuted.reason:
I'm refuting this one. I zoomed the inset rider on page 6, panel 6.5 to 6x and also checked it at print size.

1. **The moustache is not a pencil moustache.** It is dark and dense. It is shorter than on the sheet and its curl is barely there. But it is drawn in strict profile, and a moustache always looks narrower from the side.

2. **The stubble only shows when zoomed in.** At 6x there is faint grey shading on the jaw. The rider's face is only about 70 px tall in the 300 DPI render, which is under a quarter inch in print. At that size the shading just looks like a shadowed jaw, not stubble. So in print the 'captivity only' stubble rule is not visibly broken.

3. **The 'leaner, sharper face' point does not hold up.** A small profile with closed eyes is being compared with a frontal close-up in the same panel. The difference is mostly scale and angle, not a different man.

4. **He reads clearly as Nagoji.** At print size the inset matches the approved commander look: rust-red turban, long curly black hair, small gold ear stud, cream tunic, red sash, and a dark moustache. The black mare and the script beat ('a man's cheek against her mane') make the link to the present-day face beside him.

What is left is the moustache being shorter and less curled, which is too slight to matter at print size and does not change who he is.

refuted.description: A second prisoner in the chained line is drawn as a Nagoji double: thick curled moustache, long curly black hair, and a gold ear stud, the three traits that identify Nagoji. On the opening establishing panel he competes with the real Nagoji at the right edge.
refuted.reason: The figure is real but too small to matter in print. On page 1, panel 1.1, the man just left of the grey-bearded elder is at about x 770-850, y 420-500 of 1838 px wide. The reviewer's coordinates (x 860-1000) land on the elder himself. This man does have curly black hair, a curled moustache, a clean chin and a gold ear stud. Four reasons it does not count as a Nagoji double. (1) Print size: the page is 6.1 in at 300 DPI. His head is about 80 px (roughly 7 mm) and the stud is about 4-5 px (about 0.4 mm). In print it is a speck, not something a reader sees as an earring. That leaves curly hair, moustache and clean chin. (2) The bible does not reserve those traits for Nagoji. CONTINUITY.md gives Ponnan curly hair, a thick moustache and a clean chin too, and tells characters apart by costume. Several other men in this row also have moustaches and curly hair. (3) Costume and staging point clearly to the real Nagoji. The double wears a cream tunic, not Nagoji's ochre, and sits mid-row at about a third of Nagoji's size. Nagoji is the dominant foreground figure at the right: ochre tunic, bandaged hands, three-quarter back view, nearest us, exactly as the script asks. A reader will not take the small man for the narrator. (4) The bible rule cited in support (Keshavrao has 'no ear stud') applies only to Keshavrao, a named ch2-3 principal who shares close-ups with Nagoji. It does not cover anonymous extras in a wide shot. The face does look like it came from the same model, so removing the stud or adding a beard would be optional polish. It is not a major localized error.

refuted.description: In the background, Nagoji is grinning broadly, relaxed, with his wrists unbound and resting in his lap. This happens moments after the wedge in 8.3, where João has his bound hand, and it breaks both the beat and the restraint continuity from 5.3 to 8.3.
refuted.reason: I cropped and zoomed page 8, panel 8.5, around x 1150-1560 and y 1540-1960 on the 1838 px page, and the art does not show what the reviewer described. 1) There is no broad grin. The face is soft-focus and small, and at 4x and 6x zoom the mouth is closed under the moustache: no teeth and no open smile. At most the expression is neutral, or reads as a faint set of the mouth. At print size the face is about 40 px tall on the 1325 px display. 2) He is still visibly restrained. The ankle shackles and their connecting chain are clearly drawn, and both wrists are wrapped in the same cloth bands used in 5.3, 6.4 and 8.3. The hands rest together in his lap, which reads as wrists bound together rather than free hands. 3) Panel 8.3 does not tie the wrists to the stool either. There João holds the wrapped wrist while the ankles are shackled, so 8.5 matches the wrist and ankle state of the panel right before it; nothing was "unbound" between the two. The only gap is that the script's 5.3 detail, "wrists bound to its legs", is not repeated here, and João would have had to free a hand to apply the wedge anyway. 4) The script asks for "Nagoji, blurred, in the background", and the figure is out of focus behind the hands, which carry the beat. His upright, unslumped posture could be a tiny polish note at most. It does not make him look free or happy, and it is too slight to matter at print size.

refuted.description: Duarte's 'Enough.' balloon is on the far right, stacked right on top of João's off-panel 'He still holds back names.' balloon. Its tail stops in empty space beside the hanging ropes, well short of Duarte's head. Duarte's two lines end up on opposite sides of the panel with João's line between them, so 'Enough.' (the mercy beat) reads as if João said it. This is a regression: the r7 review (issue 18) put both Duarte balloons on the left beside his face, and r8 and r9 moved 'Enough.' back to the right.
refuted.reason: I checked this on crops of r9 and r7 page 8. The positions the reviewer gives are right: in r7 both Duarte balloons were on the left, and in r9 "Enough." sits top-right with João's "He still holds back names." just below it. The main claim, that "Enough." reads as João's line, does not hold up in the art. The "Enough." tail is a long wedge pointing left and slightly down, straight at Duarte's head. Duarte is the only figure in the panel and nobody else is on that side. João's balloon has its own tail, which points the opposite way (up and right) to the panel edge by the door. That is the usual sign for an off-panel speaker, so the two balloons are easy to tell apart. Reading order is also correct: "Enough." is the highest balloon, so it is read first, then João, then "A dead prisoner cannot testify." at bottom-left. That matches the script order for 8.6 (Duarte, João off, Duarte), and the mercy beat survives. A tail does not have to touch the head, only point at it. The tip stops roughly 100 display px (about 12 mm at print) short of his hair, which slightly weakens the link but does not change who is speaking. The move back to the right since r7 is real, but a change between versions is not a defect by itself. What is left is polish: the eye goes right, then right, then back left, and the tail could be longer, or "Enough." could go back beside Duarte's face on the left as in r7. That is minor, not major.

refuted.description: The wince the script demands ('Draw the wince. It matters.') is missing. Duarte sits beside Nagoji facing the camera with a calm face, eyes half-closed and lowered toward his own lap. He is not looking at the bandaged hands, and there is no flinch and no twitching fingers. Nagoji is the one studying his hands. The first sign of Duarte's conscience, which pays off in ch24-25, is lost.
refuted.reason: Under zoom, the art doesn't match the reviewer's description. The tight crop of Duarte's face in panel 3.1 (page-03.png, roughly x680-840, y370-520 at full resolution) shows knitted brows and deep creases across the forehead. His eyes are cast down and his mouth is turned down at the corners. That is a pained, troubled look, not a serene one. His head is bowed and turned toward screen right, toward Nagoji, and his gaze falls in the direction of the bandaged hands Nagoji is holding up. A reader at print size will see a grieved priest looking at the prisoner's hurt hands, which carries the conscience beat. His hands are tucked into his sleeves in his lap, which fits "fingers twitch inside his sleeves". A twitch inside a sleeve can't really be drawn in a still panel anyway. Nagoji also looking at his own hands doesn't contradict the script. A sharper flinch, with the eyes squeezed, could make the moment hit harder, but that is optional polish, not a missing beat. Since the claim is uncertain at best, it is refuted.

refuted.description: The 'Bring him' beat tells a different story. The script has Duarte rise from his crouch beside Nagoji and turn away without looking at him. Here Duarte is at the far right of a large, empty torchlit hall, with his body and lowered face angled LEFT toward Nagoji's side, so he reads as walking toward him. Nagoji is moved onto a raised stone ledge, alone, with none of the chained line from 1.1, 2.2-2.3 and 3.1. The geography breaks from the panel before.
refuted.reason:
I looked at page 3, panel 3.5 in full-resolution crops and compared it with 1.1, 2.2, 2.3, 3.1 and 4.1. The finding does not hold up as a major problem.

1. The beat lands. Duarte is standing and has gone some distance. His head is bowed and his eyes are lowered, so he is clearly not looking at Nagoji, which is the beat the script says matters: "he does not look at Nagoji while making it". The "Bring him." balloon is readable and its tail points to Duarte.

2. He does not clearly walk toward Nagoji. He faces left with his cassock trailing behind him, so he is moving left. The stair archway, the obvious way out, sits in the middle of the strip between the two men (about x=620-760 in the strip crop, with Duarte at about x=1290 and Nagoji at about x=200). The more natural reading is a priest heading for the stairs, which matches 4.2, where Duarte leads the walk. The script's "turning away" is not drawn literally, but the story does not change.

3. Part of the geography claim is wrong. The finding says 3.1 shows the chained line, but 3.1 and 3.2 already drop the line of prisoners: 3.1 shows only Nagoji, chained by the ankles to a wall bracket, with Duarte and João. Panel 3.5 keeps that setup: Nagoji alone, ankle shackles with a chain to the wall, the same ochre vest, white dhoti and bandaged wrists.

4. The set changes in every panel of this sequence. In 3.1 the stairs are at the left behind Duarte with a table at the far left. In 4.1 the stairs are at the right with barrels and a cart. So the bigger hall in 3.5 is not a one-off break.

5. The cast overrides list only Duarte as visible in 3.5, so the script never required Nagoji to be in this panel at all.

What is left is polish: Nagoji now sits on a raised stone ledge instead of the floor, and he is far from where Duarte was crouching. On a strip about one inch tall at print size he is small, and this is at most minor.

refuted.description: The script calls this hesitation 'the beat the reader must remember in chapter 24', but it is shrunk to two short half-width strips that are nearly duplicates. 8.1 does not show the jaw working ('chewing words he cannot swallow'). His mouth is closed and still, the same as in 8.2. The only difference is that his eyes drop a little further, so the nod barely reads as a separate action.
refuted.reason:
I looked at full-resolution crops of the page 8 top row: each panel is about 770x232 px at 300 DPI, roughly 2.6 x 0.8 in at print size. I also compared the two faces side by side. The two panels are not near-duplicates in the way that matters.

**8.1:** Duarte's eyes are open and looking down and to the side. His brows are knit, and his mouth is pressed shut with the corners turned down and some tension in the lower lip. That reads as a man holding back words. A single still image cannot literally show a jaw "working", and the pressed, tense mouth is a reasonable way to draw that direction.

**8.2:** His eyes are fully closed. His head drops lower and tips further forward, so his hair now touches the top border, and his face sits lower and larger in the frame. That reads clearly as the "small, weary nod".

Keeping the camera, lighting and framing the same while changing only the expression and head angle is the standard way comics draw a hesitation beat. It is deliberate, not a defect. The difference between open eyes and closed eyes with a bowed head is still visible at print scale.

On size, the script asks to "hold on him for a full panel". That means a panel of his own, which 8.1 gets. It does not ask for full width. Page 8 has the six panels the script calls for, with 8.6 as the full-width bottom strip.

The beat is on the page, Duarte is correctly identified, and nothing in it is forbidden. At most, an optional polish would be a slightly stronger jaw-clench line in 8.1. That is not a localized error of major severity.

minors.description: Duarte's face drifts from the sheet. It is broader, with a heavier jaw, fuller cheeks and heavier dark brows, where the sheet and panels 8.1 and 8.2 on the same page show a gaunt, long, hollow-cheeked face. The hair, cassock and cross keep him recognisable, but the face reads as a sturdier, younger man.
minors.evidence: Compare the 8.6 close-up (wide jaw, full cheeks) with the gaunt face in 8.1 and 8.2 directly above it and with 10-father-duarte-v15.png.

minors.description: In the long shot, Duarte's hair is brownish, not grey, and his face is smooth and younger than his fifties. Nagoji, seated far left, has straighter, shorter-looking hair than his long curly lock.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crops: Duarte at right has slicked brown-grey hair and an unlined profile. Nagoji at left has hair falling straight to his shoulders.

minors.description: Nagoji wears a gold stud in BOTH ears. The bible specifies a single small gold ear stud, and the ear varies between panels: his right ear has the stud in 1.3, 7.3 and 9.1, but in the front-on 6.5 his right ear is bare and the stud is in his left. The stud side should be locked and applied consistently.
minors.evidence: 3.3 extreme close-up: gold studs visible in both earlobes. 6.5 present-day face: viewer-left ear (his right) bare, viewer-right ear (his left) studded. 1.3 and 9.1: stud in his right ear.

minors.description: Duarte's costume is inconsistent. In 2.1, 2.2 and 6.1 he wears a shoulder cape (pellegrina) over the cassock. The approved sheet and his other appearances (4.2, 5.3, 8.3) show a plain cassock with no cape.
minors.evidence: 6.1: a short black cape over his shoulders while he reads the papers. The same cape appears in 2.1 and 2.2. In 4.2 and 5.3 he wears a capeless cassock, matching the 10-father-duarte-v15.png turnaround.

minors.description: A crackle-like mosaic texture (an upscale artifact) covers Nagoji's face, so his skin reads as pitted or scarred. The bible specifies no facial scar. The same texture shows more faintly on his face in 2.4.
minors.evidence: Zoomed 9.4: a reticulated cracked pattern across the forehead, cheeks and nose bridge, unlike the smooth skin rendering in 1.3, 6.5 and 7.4.

minors.description: Duarte wears a short black shoulder cape (pellegrina) over his cassock. The approved sheet and the bible ask for a plain cassock with a standing collar and no cape, and he has no cape on pages 4, 5, 7 and 8, so his costume switches back and forth across the chapter.
minors.evidence: 2.1: a cape-like layer over his shoulders as he goes down ahead of João. 2.2: the same cape edge across his shoulders and upper arms. Compare 4.2, 5.3, 7.2 and 8.3, where he wears the plain buttoned cassock with a sash, as on 10-father-duarte-v15.png.

minors.description: Nagoji's neighbours in the chained line change between two consecutive panels of the same moment.
minors.evidence: 2.2: next to Nagoji are a bare-chested, grey-bearded elder and then a curly-haired man. 2.3: next to him are a younger dark-bearded man in grey rags and a bald man.

minors.description: Two problems in 3.5. Duarte wears the shoulder cape again, and his face reads younger and smoother, with brownish hair rather than the gaunt, lined grey-haired priest. Nagoji has also moved from the floor in 3.1 to a raised stone bench in a differently laid-out hall.
minors.evidence: 3.5, right: cape over the shoulders, smooth jaw, brown-grey slicked hair (about x 1400-1520, y 2310-2400). 3.5, left: Nagoji sits on a stone ledge with a wall chain and the stair is now centred through an arch. In 3.1 he sits cross-legged on the floor with the stair behind Duarte at left.

minors.description: The script asks for a mouth that is cracked and rust-dark. The drawn lips are smooth and healthy, so the only facial sign of captivity is lost.
minors.evidence: 3.3 full-width mouth close-up: full, unbroken lips with no cracking or dried-blood darkening. Script 3.3: 'Tight on Nagoji's mouth, cracked and rust-dark.'

minors.description: Prop continuity on the walk. Duarte carries a lit torch in 4.2, and it is gone in 4.4 a few steps later. In 4.2 João walks beside Nagoji, not behind him as the script says.
minors.evidence: 4.2: Duarte holds a burning torch in his raised left hand, and João is level with Nagoji at the left. 4.4: Duarte walks with empty hands toward the red doorway.

minors.description: Nagoji's cream dhoti changes length. It is ankle-length in 4.2, then a ragged knee-length cut-off in 5.3 and 6.2, then full-length again in 6.4.
minors.evidence: 4.2: the dhoti falls to the ankle irons. 5.3 and 6.2: the hem is torn at mid-calf to knee and reads as shorts. 6.4: full white cloth over the legs again.

minors.description: Duarte's shoulder cape appears again. This is the chapter's largest Duarte panel, so the departure from the approved plain cassock is most visible here.
minors.evidence: 6.1: a clear black capelet layer over his shoulders above the buttoned cassock, while he reads the papers.

minors.description: The interrogation set changes within the page. In 5.3 and 6.2 Nagoji is tied to a backless stool, and in 6.4 he sits in an armchair with his wrists roped to its arms. The brazier on a tall stand at the right in 6.2 becomes a low floor brazier in the centre, and the tool table moves from left of Nagoji to the far right.
minors.evidence: 6.2: backless stool, table at left, tall brazier at right. 6.4: rope coiled round chair armrests at both wrists, low brazier at the bottom centre, João at a table at the far right.

minors.description: In the Kanka memory, the turbaned rider has a thin, short moustache and chin stubble rather than Nagoji's thick curled moustache, so he only loosely reads as Nagoji. Where the red sash dissolves into the ink spatter it leaves red flecks on the white tunic that can read as blood.
minors.evidence: Left third of 6.5: the rider's moustache is a short dark strip, unlike the curled moustache on the present-day face beside it. Red sash fragments scatter over the cream sleeve at the lower edge (about x 480-650, y 2470-2540).

minors.description: The brazier changes design within the page. It is a small basket brazier on short legs in 8.3 and a large iron cauldron of coals with scroll handles in 8.5. It also differs from the braziers in 5.1, 5.3 and 6.2.
minors.evidence: 8.3: a small round grate on three legs, upper left. 8.5: a wide, deep iron bowl with curled iron handles filling the lower right.

minors.description: A coarse dark blanket appears pulled up over Nagoji's lower face. It is not present when he is back in his place in 9.1, so the prop has no setup.
minors.evidence: 9.1: Nagoji sits against the wall with his arms on his knees and no blanket. 9.4: a thick, rough dark cloth fills the lower third of the frame and covers his mouth and moustache.

minors.description: Nagoji's hand bandages carry large rust-red patches across the knuckles and backs of the hands. They read as dried blood soaking through, which conflicts with the standing rule against blood. The aftermath can be shown with grime, grey-brown stains and posture without blood-red seepage. Page 3 panel 1 has the same red-brown blotching on a smaller scale.
minors.evidence: page-09.png panel 1, both wrapped hands at about x 800-1080, y 650-900 in original pixels. page-03.png panel 1, hands at about x 860-1110, y 555-720.

minors.description: In the ink-splatter dissolve that bleeds the Kanka memory into the dungeon, the red of Nagoji's sash breaks into red droplet fragments along the bottom edge. In a panel about a horse that was shot, those red flecks can read as blood spray. The splatter should stay grey and black, with the red ending cleanly at the sash.
minors.evidence: page-06.png panel 5, the bottom-centre of the flashback at about x 480-780, y 2380-2540 in original pixels, where the red sash breaks into speckles inside the grey splatter.

minors.description: The ledger entry '17 prisioneiro marata' (scripted) is set in a clean modern book-serif italic and sits in the middle of the left page. The quill nib is writing on the far right page, nowhere near the entry. It reads as a typeset label rather than a clerk's fresh, still-wet handwriting, and the hand is not writing it. Use a period hand-lettered script, placed where the nib is.
minors.evidence: page-01.png panel 2: the entry is at about x 445-725, y 1415-1450 in original pixels, and the quill tip is at about x 1250-1290, y 1480-1500.

minors.description: Nagoji is wearing silver rings on the fingers of both bandaged hands. Neither the continuity bible nor the captivity sheet gives him rings (his only jewellery is the small gold ear stud), and a prisoner would have been stripped of them. Remove the rings.
minors.evidence: page-03.png panel 1: metallic rings on the index and middle fingers of both hands at about x 860-1110, y 555-640 in original pixels.

minors.description: The framing differs from the script. The script asks for Nagoji's face in profile lit by the red glow from the doorway. minors.description: The script asks for a tight shot of the mouth, 'cracked and rust-dark'. The lips here are smooth, full and closed, yet two speech balloons come from them.

minors.description: Nagoji should be 'not in the room', with eyes unfocused, in a small panel. The art gives a full-width strip with a sharp, alert sideways glance, which reads as Nagoji watching someone in the room, not drifting to the Godavari.

minors.description: The establishing shot drifts from the script. Nagoji is drawn in three-quarter FRONT view looking back over his shoulder, not 'three-quarter back view'. No slit window high up is visible as the failing light source, and the wall is straight, not curved.

minors.description: Duarte's 'Enough.' and Joao's off-panel 'He still holds back names.' are stacked tightly together on the right, while Duarte's closing line sits apart on the left. Two speakers' balloons nest together, and the reader's eye zigzags right then back left for the final line.

minors.description: The chapter title 'Dungeons of Goa' is repeated at chapter-opener size above every page, not only page 1. Every page reads as a new chapter opening and loses vertical space. The script does not call for a running head.
